labels.description: Tariffs and retaliatory counter measures are elevated into the headline, and the body adds proposed additional export controls and tariffs, supply chain limits on access to rare earth minerals and other raw materials, tariff-driven cost, pricing, market access and profitability effects, and the cost and fines or reputational harm of complying with rapidly changing tariffs, while the revenue share outside the U.S. stays at about 56 percent (2024 to 2025 roll-forward) and the sanctions reference drops "in certain conflict zones".
labels.rationale: criterion 1: new exposures are disclosed (rare earth and raw material access, tariff compliance cost and penalty risk), and criterion 3 applies because the scope widens from imposed controls to proposed additional tariffs and the stated consequence widens from business and supply chain to business, financial condition and results of operations.

labels.description: The PFAS manufacturing exit moves from "progressing toward the exit of all PFAS manufacturing by the end of 2025" to "completed its exit of PFAS manufacturing at the end of 2025", with new disclosure of ongoing water treatment and remediation of residual PFAS, asset and facility disposition (dismantling, cleaning, repurposing) and discussions over leased facilities, while the $897 million 2018 State of Minnesota settlement example is dropped, pending PFAS suits now include international jurisdictions, and asset retirement obligations become charges for ongoing asset use, retirement or disposition.
labels.rationale: criterion 3: a planned exit becomes realized and the exit timing and feasibility risks are removed, plus criterion 2 and criterion 4 for the dropped $897 million Minnesota settlement and the added international litigation, and criterion 1 for the new post-exit remediation and asset disposition exposures.

labels.description: The paragraph on artificial intelligence development, use and regulation is removed and replaced by a new paragraph on risks as a direct and indirect supplier to the U.S. and other governments (procurement compliance, government audit, investigation and termination rights, uncertain federal funding, False Claims Act liability, suspension or debarment), and customers are added to the parties whose conduct is covered.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: a previously disclosed risk (artificial intelligence) is removed and a new exposure (government contracting) is disclosed, which also triggers criterion 2 for the dropped AI regulation reference and the new government procurement programs.
